description: NATURAL JOIN incorrectly requires an ON clause. In ANSI SQL, NATURAL JOIN (and CROSS JOIN) should not have an ON or USING clause. The current implementation only exempts CROSS JOIN, causing a parse error for valid NATURAL JOIN statements.
suggested_fix: Change the condition to check for both 'cross and 'natural: (if (memq jtype '(cross natural)) (parser-pure #f) (parser-then (sql-keyword "ON") lazy-sql-expr))

description: render-hex-board will crash if the board is empty. It calls (apply min ...) and (apply max ...) on a list of coordinates. If the board has no tiles, board-tiles returns an empty list, and applying min/max to an empty list is an error in Scheme.
suggested_fix: Add a check for (null? coords) before calculating bounds, or provide default values based on the 'radius metadata if the board is empty.

description: The choice modifier parser only captures the first 'when' or 'do' modifier. Since it uses assq on the list of modifiers, subsequent modifiers of the same type (e.g., multiple effects in one choice) are silently ignored.
code_snippet:
(let ([guard-mod (assq 'when mods)]
      [do-mod (assq 'do mods)])
     ;; Build flat list: (-> label target :when guard :do effect)
suggested_fix: Filter the 'mods' list to collect all 'do' effects into a list, or update the AST to support multiple modifiers of the same type.

description: The parse-number function only matches sequences of digits, meaning it cannot parse floating-point numbers. This restricts Chronicle variables and guards to integer values only.
suggested_fix: Update the parser to handle an optional decimal point and subsequent digits: (parser-bind (parser-seq (some digit) (optional (parser-then (char #\.) (some digit)) '())) ...)

description: The string-replace helper function is incorrectly implemented; it only replaces characters, as it only checks the first character of the 'old' string argument. It will fail or behave unexpectedly if used for multi-character string replacement.
code_snippet:
(define (string-replace str old new)
  (list->string
   (map (lambda (c) (if (char=? c (string-ref old 0)) (string-ref new 0) c))
        (string->list str))))
suggested_fix: Rename the function to char-replace or implement a proper string substitution algorithm that handles multi-character patterns.
